stem:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

City trees are often praised as natural air conditioners, but their cooling effect depends on more than simply planting them. A broad canopy shades roads and buildings, reducing the amount of solar heat absorbed by surfaces during the day. Trees also release water vapour through their leaves; this process can lower nearby air temperatures, although it works best when the soil has enough moisture. Together, shade and evaporation can make a tree-lined street more comfortable during hot weather.

The benefits are not distributed evenly. Neighbourhoods with fewer trees may have more paved surfaces, which absorb and retain heat. Residents there can face greater exposure to high temperatures, particularly when homes lack effective cooling. Planting programmes can help address this difference, but young trees need regular watering and protection if they are to survive. A plan that counts saplings at the moment of planting may therefore overstate its lasting success.

Urban forestry also involves practical choices. Trees must suit local conditions, and their roots and branches need room to grow without damaging pavements or interfering with overhead infrastructure. This does not make planting a poor response to urban heat. Rather, it suggests that successful programmes combine suitable species, careful placement and long-term maintenance. The value of a city’s tree cover lies not only in how many trees it has, but also in whether those trees can thrive where people most need their benefits.

What is the central idea of the passage?
options: City trees reduce heat most effectively when planting is carefully planned and maintained.
Urban trees are generally unsuitable because their roots and branches damage infrastructure.
Neighbourhoods with paved surfaces should replace them entirely with tree-covered areas.
Counting newly planted saplings is the most reliable way to measure urban cooling.

verdicts.working: The passage explains trees’ cooling benefits and emphasizes suitable species, careful placement, and long-term maintenance.
